idiom_name: JUnit 5 @Test + src/test/resources golden files, hand-written compare/update
implementation_notes: JUnit 5 is a runner and assertion library, not a snapshot store, so the record/compare/approve loop is hand-written: read the expected artefact from src/test/resources via getResourceAsStream or a project-relative Path, capture the subject's output as String or byte[], compare with assertEquals (JUnit renders the diff) and gate rewriting behind a system property or a dedicated recorder test. Use @ParameterizedTest for the input corpus and @TempDir for anything the subject writes, and fix Locale.ROOT plus an explicit timezone so formatting is machine-independent. The hand-written form is the Java norm and stays justified when resources must live on the test classpath.
pitfalls: Classpath resources are read-only inside the built jar; the update path must write the source-tree location explicitly, and confusing the two turns re-recording into a no-op or a build failure.
Locale, timezone and default charset leak into String.format/new String(bytes); set Locale.ROOT and Charset explicitly in the harness.
Large golden resources ship in the test artifact and are read fully into memory; keep them small and per-case.

variants.name: ApprovalTests.java with approved/received files
variants.implementation_notes: ApprovalTests.java supplies the workflow: Approvals.verify(value) serializes the value, writes a received file, compares it with the approved file and reports a diff for a human to accept or reject; the library is part of the multi-language ApprovalTests family whose site is approvaltests.com. Choose it when several JVM projects share the harness or when the team wants the approve/reject ceremony standardized; it still needs the same normalization (locale, ordering, volatile fields) that a hand-written comparator does.
pitfalls: Received files are written into the source tree by default; keep *.received.* out of version control and make CI fail instead of accepting.
Default object serialization via toString pins types and field order; supply an explicit formatter for the observable projection.
